title: I Let the Neighbor's Christmas Lights Timer Hit the HOA Dark-Sky Letter He Signed

parts.text: I walked the dog at 11:07 p.m. and Dale's roof still strobed like a used-car lot. In March he had circulated a dark-sky letter about my porch bulb. I was thirty-four, first-floor condo, holding a leash and the PDF he had asked me to sign. The letter banned decorative lighting after 10. Dale's display had a timer labeled DUSK TO DAWN in silver Sharpie. I filmed the timer, the clock on my phone, and the letterhead with his signature. Then I emailed the architectural committee from the same address Dale had used to scold me. At 11:19 a committee reply bounced to the thread: we will inspect tonight.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: The committee is coming while his dusk-to-dawn box is still lit.

social.video_title: He wrote the dark-sky letter and left the roof on until dawn — Part 1/2
social.description: March petition, December strobe, a timer in Sharpie. I forwarded his own letterhead. Would you have waited until January?

parts.text: The inspector stood in the street with a lux meter like it was a traffic stop. Dale said holiday spirit was different. The letter did not have a spirit exception. They tagged the display. Dale recircuited to 9:55 p.m. and taped a note that said community first. I put my porch bulb on a 9:50 timer so we could match. The dog still pees at 11. The roof does not strobe. Dale waves now with a smaller smile. I keep the PDF. Dark sky was his idea. I just believed him in December.

social.video_title: The lux meter does not do holiday spirit — Part 2/2
social.description: Tagged display, 9:55 cutoff, matching porch bulb. Was a petition a seasonal mood?
